2.1.2.1-f17.accuracy_reason: Horace, Odes 3.6.6 does read 'hinc omne principium, huc refer exitum', and the lines are about the gods.

2.1.2.1-f20.accuracy_reason: The words come from Minucius's speech at Livy 22.14, not book 23, and the note hedges the correction suitably.

2.1.2.1-f5.accuracy_reason: Persius 3.65 reads 'quid opus Cratero magnos promittere montis?', and Craterus was a well-known physician. The note's reading of the point is right.

2.1.2.1-f6.accuracy_reason: Horace, Odes 3.1.17–21 is about Damocles' sword hanging over a guilty neck, and the standard text reads 'citharaeque'.
